mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) and a drop in consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in the housing and retail sectors, which triggers a negative sentiment shift in equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing supply chain disruption (indicated by INDPRO below 100), the resulting production bottlenecks reduce corporate profit margins and increase input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 100, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% yoy, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past three months indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is increasing, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous slowdown in real GDP growth (GDPC1) and a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad economic deceleration that reduces corporate revenue expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1.0% and HOUST decline > 0.5% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth is below 1.0% and HOUST declines by more than 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer demand (RSAFS above 700,000 million dollars), the resulting corporate revenue growth drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS exceeds 700000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
